The base map view could not be created. The screen stays here instead of taking the app down with it. It is usually a mistyped key, or a product that was not enabled in the console — check the key and restart the app.

Wander around the anchor point so the track looks human.
Neutralises isFromMockProvider/isMock, the mock_location setting and the AppOps check, so detectors see nothing.
Denies WiFi scans, cell information and raw GNSS (NMEA, measurements). Without those inputs an app cannot compute a real fix of its own and fall back to it.
Hooks the Amap, Baidu and Tencent location SDKs directly — including the instances the app loads on its own. Needed for apps that read their position from a map SDK instead of the system.

Answers the city, province, district and address getters of the map SDKs with the values resolved for the anchor by the map picker. Apps that display the city name a location SDK reports need this: with the address left real, or left empty, they keep showing where you really are. Turn it off if an app misbehaves.
City not resolved — open the map picker and save once
Shapes the forged position itself — accuracy, altitude, speed and drift — and what a detector is able to see. Each switch writes to the config as you flip it.

The picker draws with Tencent’s base map, and looks addresses up through the system geocoder. The module itself forges positions and needs no map key at all — this page only affects the “pick on a map” screen.
This build bundles one renderer, Tencent, and ships no key of its own. Paste your own Tencent key below; the setup steps are in the next card.
No key yet; the picker will show an empty map until you add one.
Needed only when that key has key signing switched on: without the matching secret, Tencent rejects every request with status 111. Leave blank otherwise.
A key change takes effect after this app is restarted: the SDK reads its key once, at launch.
What the console will ask for

Tencent Location Service binds a key to this package name and this signing certificate. Differ by one character and the key is rejected — with an error that looks exactly like a wrong key. Copy these two values instead of retyping them.

%1$s keeps its setup steps below. These consoles are redesigned often; if a menu has moved, the thread is always the same — application management, create an application, fill in the package name and SHA-1.

1. Sign in to Tencent Location Services, then Console → Application management → My applications.
2. Create an application, then add a Key under it.
3. Enable the products you need: Android SDK, plus WebService API for the HTTP interfaces such as reverse geocoding.
4. Enter the package name and the SHA-1.
5. Copy the resulting Key into the Tencent field above.
Keys stay on this device, in the module’s own preferences, and are sent only to the platform’s own servers by that platform’s SDK.
